questions.stem: Explain why it is important to make requirements testable.
markingGuide: Testable requirements ensure that the system can be verified against the requirements.
They reduce ambiguity and help avoid misinterpretations.
Testable requirements facilitate the creation of test cases.
questions.explanation: Making requirements testable is crucial because it allows for the verification of whether the system meets the specified requirements. This reduces ambiguity and misinterpretations, ensuring that developers and testers have a clear understanding of what needs to be achieved. Additionally, testable requirements help in creating effective test cases.

questions.stem: Describe the MoSCoW prioritization technique and its categories.
markingGuide: MoSCoW is a prioritization technique used to categorize requirements.
Must have: Critical requirements essential for the system to work.
Should have: Important but not critical requirements.
Could have: Desirable requirements that enhance user experience.
Won't have: Requirements not implemented in the current release.
questions.explanation: The MoSCoW technique is a method for prioritizing requirements by categorizing them into four levels: Must have (critical requirements essential for system functionality), Should have (important but not critical requirements), Could have (desirable features that enhance user experience), and Won't have (requirements that are not included in the current release).
